chunk.chapter_title: 106. In spite of entreaties Shri Ram remains steadfast in his vow
chunk.text:
THE R.AMAYANA OF VALMIKI 
" 0 Brother, it is not meet to grieve for the king, who, full 
of years, having enjoyed the pleasures of the world, respected 
by the good, has given up his life. Having abandoned his 
worn-out frame, he has obtained the form of a celestial being. 
"A wise, learned and colightened man like thee, should not 
grieve for such a site. Exercising patience, thou shouldst cease 
to lament and giving up sorrow return to the capital. 0 Chief 
among the Eloquent, thy father has commanded thee to dwell 
in Ayodhya. I too will perform the behests of him who ever 
practised righteousness I 
" I cannot disregard the commands of my illustrious father, 
he is worthy to he obeyed by thee and me, being our parent 
and our ruler. 0 Son of R.sghu, I shall, therefore, obey his will 
and dwell in the forest. 0 Chief of Men, those who desite 
felicity in a future state, and who are virtuous and benevolent 
should obey their elders. 0 Great One, bear in mind the 
behests of our father, a lover of truth, and return to the capital 
to rule over the kingdom ! " 
The magnanimous R.ama, having uttered these sage words 
relative to the need for obedience to his father, heeame silent.

" 0 Prince of Raghu, like the gods, thou an magnanimous,

Having spoken thus, Bharata continued : " 0 Rams, be

I am bound by the ties of duty, else would I have slain my

brief.summary_1line: Bharata pleads passionately for Rama to return and rule Ayodhya, but Rama remains firm in his vow to honor their father's command and stay in exile.

image_candidates.scene_text: Bharata bows with his head at Rama’s feet in the forest, pleading for him to return while sages, citizens, and weeping women look on.
Rama stands calm and resolute in ascetic garb beneath forest trees while Bharata argues before him with folded hands.
A gathered crowd of brahmins, merchants, priests, and grieving mothers raise their voices together, begging Rama to return to Ayodhya.

deep.rich_summary: Bharata pleads passionately with Rama to abandon his exile and return to Ayodhya to rule. He praises Rama’s wisdom, restraint, and spiritual insight, arguing that a prince whose duty is to protect the people should not withdraw to the forest. Bharata condemns the circumstances created by Kaikeyi and suggests that their father Dasharatha, near death and troubled, made a misguided decision under pressure. Declaring himself too young and unworthy to rule, Bharata begs Rama to accept the crown, even offering to serve him as a subordinate. Despite Bharata’s humility and the collective appeals of priests, citizens, and elders, Rama remains unwavering in his vow to obey his father’s command. The episode highlights Rama’s absolute commitment to dharma and filial obedience, a defining moral principle of the epic.

highlight_spans.why: Rama frames death and duty philosophically, urging restraint in grief and acceptance of destiny.
Rama’s central principle: he refuses to disregard his father’s command, establishing the moral core of the episode.
Bharata’s anguish over his mother Kaikeyi’s actions reveals his moral conflict and emotional suffering.
Bharata argues that a warrior’s first duty is to rule and protect the people, challenging Rama’s decision.
The emotional climax where Bharata bows at Rama’s feet and begs him to show compassion.
The closing moment emphasizing Rama’s unwavering fidelity to his vow despite universal pleading.
